name: True Memory

paper.title: Storage Is Not Memory: A Retrieval-Centered Architecture for Agent Recall

construction.processing: write message row + FTS5 and 256-d vector rows; encoding gate disabled in benchmarks
construction.writer: L1 writer (no LLM); gate uses gzip novelty, salience, prediction error

organization.structure: flat event table plus derived side tables
organization.stores: single SQLite file: messages, summaries, timelines, entity profiles, surprise scores
organization.index: FTS5 BM25 + sqlite-vec 256-d dense (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B or Model2Vec)

management.operations: L4 consolidator writes cluster summaries, contradiction records, timeline rows
management.conflicts: contradiction records by entity/predicate; superseded-by timeline links

retrieval.query: question; HyDE expansion in Pro tier
retrieval.candidates: FTS5 BM25 top-k + dense top-k, weighted RRF (k=60)
retrieval.selection: temporal/engram/surprise reweighting, cross-encoder rerank of top 100

use.reasoning: single gpt-4.1-mini answer call, max 200 tokens

stages.ingestion: An encoding gate (gzip-based novelty, salience, embedding prediction error) admits or rejects each event; it is disabled (every event admitted) in all reported benchmark numbers. Admitted events are written verbatim to a SQLite messages table with FTS5 and 256-d sqlite-vec indices.
stages.construction: Post-ingestion batch jobs build an L5 per-event surprise score and an L0 speaker engram (preference attribute map + char-n-gram style vector).
stages.organization: Single SQLite file: verbatim messages plus side tables (summaries, contradiction records, timelines, entity profiles, surprise scores, episodes).
stages.update: L4 consolidator produces cluster summaries, contradiction records and timeline rows with superseded-by links, kept alongside the verbatim events.
stages.retrieval: FTS5 BM25 and dense top-k fused by weighted RRF (k=60), reweighted by conditional temporal boost, speaker-engram prior and surprise boost, then cross-encoder rerank (pre-rerank window 100) with modality factor; top-k (default 10) to the answer model. Pro tier adds HyDE query expansion.
stages.answer: gpt-4.1-mini answers from the retrieved top-k (temperature 0, max 200 tokens).

summary: Retrieval-centered memory over verbatim events in a single SQLite file (BM25+dense RRF, salience/engram reweighting, cross-encoder rerank), arguing extraction at ingestion is the wrong primitive.
notes:
Authors: Joshua Adler, Guy Zehavi (Sauron Labs). Three tiers: Edge (Model2Vec potion-base-8M + ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2), Base (Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B@256d + gte-reranker-modernbert-base), Pro (= Base + HyDE query expansion). All scores use a semantic-match judge that the authors say is more lenient than strict-match; absolute numbers not comparable to strict-match baselines. AXES-CHECK: seed taxonomy row consistent; paper adds an ingestion gate (disabled in benchmarks), L3 salience/L0 speaker-prior reweighting and HyDE (Pro) at selection time.
DESIGN: Sec 4.1 (Stages 1-10), 5, 5.2, 6 (Table 1). forgetting null: no deletion described; control.management null: consolidator mechanism (LLM or rule) not stated.
